items.title: 4 High Yield Stocks That Have Never Missed a Dividend Payment
items.summary: Recessions, oil crashes, and a pandemic failed to interrupt the quarterly checks from four household-name payers. But an unbroken record is a lower bar than it sounds, so we stress-tested each one on cash flow and debt before trusting the next payment.

items.title: FAA Chief Warns System ‘Will Continue to Break.’ AT&T, Verizon, and Lumen Could Be Big Winners
items.summary: When the nation's top aviation regulator admits the air traffic system is guaranteed to fail again, someone gets paid to fix it. One telecom giant already holds a foothold in the contract, and its stock may be pricing in far too little.

items.title: How Much Does a 65-Year-Old Need Invested in Dividend Stocks to Collect $2,000 a Month?
items.summary: Three popular high-yield stocks promise a steady retirement paycheck, but one has a thin cash cushion and another has slashed its payout before. Which one could quietly shrink your monthly income when you can least afford it?

items.title: How Retirees Can Turn $175,000 Into Passive Income With These 4 Dividend Stocks
items.summary: Selling shares to cover bills means accepting whatever price the market offers that month. Four dividend payers from four sectors could replace that gamble, but one of them has already slashed its payout once, and each carries a risk worth knowing.

items.title: AT&T vs. Verizon: Which Telecom Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: AT&T and Verizon both trade at similar valuations, but their paths diverge sharply in other areas.

items.title: A $1 Million Dividend Portfolio Could Pay You $40,000 a Year. A Roth IRA Changes What You Keep
items.summary: Two retirees can collect identical dividends from identical stocks and still walk away with very different paychecks. The gap depends on which account holds the shares, and for payers like AGNC and Ares Capital it compounds into a surprisingly costly mistake.
